subject.title: fix(agents): preserve runtime tool inheritance tokens

question: Should OpenClaw preserve policy-filtered MCP/LSP runtime selector tokens in spawned child inherited allowlists after this branch is rebased onto current main?
rationale: The central code path decides which tool-capability selectors cross a spawned-session authorization boundary; automation can review the patch shape but cannot own the final security-policy acceptance for the refreshed merge result.

options.title: Accept After Rebase
options.body: Resolve conflicts and land the selector-preservation approach after confirming the refreshed diff still filters selectors through profile, agent, group, subagent, inherited, runtime allow, and deny policy layers.

options.title: Move Filtering Boundary
options.body: Replace this branch with an owner-authored fix nearer final MCP/LSP materialization if maintainers prefer not to persist selector tokens in inherited session state.

options.title: Pause For Broader Tool Policy Design
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers want to solve MCP selector inheritance together with broader tool-visibility and strict-inheritance work.

recommendation.title: Accept After Rebase
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts and land the selector-preservation approach after confirming the refreshed diff still filters selectors through profile, agent, group, subagent, inherited, runtime allow, and deny policy layers.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main commits touch the affected agent, gateway, and embedded-runner paths, and this security-boundary choice needs maintainer-level owner review after rebase.
